On Thu, Mar 9, 2017 at 12:23 PM, EMA <grassl...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi unmarked gurus,

I'm trying to use the simHDSopen function to simulate data for a power analysis that will inform a monitoring strategy for birds.  Things seem to go well when I create the 4-D array if I use the default value for maximum distance (B=3) in simHDSopen; in fact, most values below 5 work fine.  But when I try large values, I get the error: 

Error in data[, "d"] : no 'dimnames' attribute for array

after running the loop to fill y4d.  I'd like to play around with different distances of point radii realistic for bird surveys (e.g., 100 m, 200 m, etc.), but when I set B to anything like those, I always get the error.  I've noticed that the error is always associated with simHDSopen generating at least one matrix in "data" (tmp$data) that has only NA values (in other words, if there is at least one row in each data matrix with numbers, the y4d loop works).  What am I missing here?  Why does creating the 4-D array fail when B is large?  I imagine I have some unrealistic parameter value in simHDSopen, but I'm not seeing it.

Here's what I'm doing:


> rm(list=ls(all=TRUE))
> tmp <-
+ simHDSopen(type="point",    # "line" or "point"
+            nsites = 10,   #
+            mean.lam = 10,   # avg density on natural scale (I think this is more like abundance at one site)
+            beta.lam = 0,   # coef of log(density) on site covariate
+            mean.sig = 1,   # avg det fucntion parameter (natural scale)
+            beta.sig = 0,   # coef of log(sigma) on obs covariate
+            B = 100,          # max distance (or maybe half-width)
+            discard0=FALSE,  # keep or discard sites with no detections
+            nreps=2,        # number of replicate DS surveys within a period of closure (seasons, years)
+            phi=1,        
+            nyears=1,       # number of primary periods
+            beta.trend =0 ) # loglinear trend of density/abundance (-0.05)

> for(yr in 1:nyears){
+   for(rep in 1:K){
+     data <- tmp$data[[yr]][[rep]]
+     site <- data[,1]
+     dclass <- data[,"d"]%/%delta + 1
+     ndclass <- B%/%delta
+     dclass <- factor(dclass, levels= 1:ndclass)
+     y4d[1:nsites,1:nD,rep,yr] <- table(site, dclass)
+   }
+ }
Error in data[, "d"] : no 'dimnames' attribute for array

I've noticed also that I can get the y4d loop to work if I set mean.lam very high (~2000 for the B=100 example above), but unless I'm missing something, that's unrealistic.  Messing with other values doesn't seem to help.

Thanks for all the work you guys put in pointing folks in the right direction!

one obvious problem is your value of mean.sig is way way too low. A value of 1 doesn't make sense with a sample range out to 100 units.... so try 20 or 50 or something and see if that works...
regards
andy
